solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Move effortlessly backwards to keep a new job, becoming happy

indicators.note: to keep means the reversed word holds the following letters inside it
backwards means the word for moving effortlessly is read from right to left

parts.note: to surf is to move effortlessly, as over waves or the web

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of job are made fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone glides along, takes up a fresh job, and cheers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move effortlessly' reads as part of the surface story; it is the synonym the reversal works on. 'becoming' is only a link to the definition, and the word is Lewis Carroll's coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll coined this word in Jabberwocky for joyous delight, and dictionaries gloss it as gleeful or happy.

clue.text: Some supporters up for recapturing the past

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
some means only part of the word supporters is used

explanation.surface: A few backers stand up for nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ORTER from inside supporters, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles imitate or recall fashions of earlier decades, harking back to bygone times.

clue.text: Be fast to catch hybrid hawk

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to catch means the word for fast holds the hybrid inside

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
a liger is a hybrid of a lion and a tigress

explanation.surface: Advice to grab a crossbred bird of prey quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird the hybrid is; it is the definition, a warmonger. A liger is the offspring of a lion and a tigress.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk in politics favours aggressive policy, and an aggressive, warlike person can be called this as a noun.

clue.text: Flier breaking rind with dove

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of the two words are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the setter's fodder, which should supply a B where it has a D

explanation.surface: A bird smashing its way through peel alongside a pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the anagram signal, but RIND + DOVE has letters D, D, E, I, N, O, R, V: the setter has slipped, as the answer needs a B in place of one D.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American warbler or South American bird named for its domed nest, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Study insurers in negotiating new business

indicators.note: negotiating suggests the letters work their way round into a new order

explanation.surface: Looking into insurers while bargaining over a fresh venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiating' rearranges all fifteen letters of STUDY INSURERS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunrise industry is a new and fast-growing sector, so its firms are fresh enterprise.

clue.text: Second aristo gets through, being superior

parts.note: a nob is slang for an aristocrat or toff
by can mean through, as in by means of

explanation.surface: Another aristocrat gets past, acting haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: NOB is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: A snobby person acts superior, looking down on others as beneath them.

clue.text: Old government council thus, one kept in check

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: kept in means the letter for one is held within the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A council of thus; one under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old government council' is a single definition: the councils of the USSR gave the state its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was a council in the former USSR, and the word came to name its government.

clue.text: Bird's 'oller

definitions.meaning: holler with its aitch dropped, as a Cockney would say it, is a howl with its aitch dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'oller shows a dropped H: holler is HOWL, and dropping its H the same way gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal bird of prey hoots, and a howl, said with the Cockney dropped aitch, is the same word as the bird.

clue.text: Beating on feet ain't so bad? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A protest that foot-beating isn't so terrible, quickly corrected as mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges AINTSOBAD; the apostrophe gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado is a torture or punishment of caning the soles of the feet.

clue.text: Fight lost at the front by English PM

indicators.note: lost at the front means the word for fight drops its first letter

parts.note: a battle is a fight

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister of England loses a battle at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost at the front' takes B off BATTLE, leaving ATTLE. Clement Attlee was UK Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain's Labour government after the Second World War as Prime Minister.

clue.text: Spark produced, perhaps, though love isn't extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters are put out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A spark is struck, though the romance is unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spark' looks like a flash of love; it is Muriel Spark, Scottish author of The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie. 'extraordinary' rearranges LOVEISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel Spark wrote and published fiction, so her trade was writing long prose works.

clue.text: Cap, one's a hat!

parts.note: to cap is to top, to outdo
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Excitement over a cap that turns out to be a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like the headwear; here it is the verb meaning to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet once worn in India, so it is headwear.

clue.text: Overalls ruin a welly, for Spooner

indicators.note: for Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: to soil is to ruin, and soil a said quickly sounds like soiler
a welly, short for wellington, is a rubber boot

explanation.surface: Muddy work clothes spoil one's wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Spooner' swaps the opening sounds of SOILER BOOT, giving BOILER SOOT, which is how the answer is said. A welly is the British word for a rubber wellington boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler suit is a one-piece garment worn over clothes for dirty work, the same as overalls.

clue.text: Diner beginning to get into spin, seeing busty lass

indicators.note: into means the diner and the first letter go inside the word for spin

parts.note: a swirl is a spinning movement
a diner is someone eating, an eater

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of get is used

explanation.surface: A diner starts to get dizzy and spots a buxom woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' looks like an American restaurant; it is a person eating. Sweater girl is 1940s slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweater girl is mid-century slang for a buxom young woman in a tight jumper, a pin-up type.

clue.text: In half-complete research, try to practise

indicators.note: in means the word for try goes inside the half word
half-complete means only the first half of research is used

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: Unfinished research, an attempt at practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like attempt; here it is what a judge does with a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go through a performance in preparation, which is practising it.

clue.text: Get down from one

parts.note: the soft feathers used for quilts, called eiderdown, come from this sea bird, so you get down from one

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb off something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' reads as dismount; it is the feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eiderdown, the soft breast feathers used for quilts, is plucked from this sea bird's nest.

clue.text: Produced round, edible sphere

indicators.note: round means the word for produced is turned around

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: Made into a round, a ball you can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a description of the cheese; it is the reversal signal on MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese made in a ball shape with a red wax coat.

clue.text: US city caging a hunter

indicators.note: caging means the city holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital city of Georgia, USA

explanation.surface: An American city traps a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caging' puts A inside ATLANTA after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Atalanta is the swift huntress of Greek myth, who joined the Calydonian boar hunt.

clue.text: Mown plant border

indicators.note: mown means cut down, here cutting off the plant's first letter

parts.note: sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground

explanation.surface: A trimmed hedge marks the edge of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mown' cuts the top off SEDGE, removing S.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the boundary or rim of something, the same as its border.

clue.text: Country outstanding at swimming

indicators.note: outstanding read as out-standing means the country stands outside the word at

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country excels in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; split it as out-standing, the country standing outside the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is a formal word for the act or art of swimming.

clue.text: Quick as a croc?

definitions.meaning: describing something given to snapping its jaws, as a crocodile does

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: crocodiles snap their jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means brisk and fast, and also inclined to snap, which a crocodile famously does.

clue.text: Mythical beast in mystical trance? Nonsense!

indicators.note: mystical suggests the letters are transformed into an obscure new order

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Claiming a mythical creature appeared in a mystic trance is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mystical' rearranges TRANCE as CRETAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan Bull of Greek myth fathered the Minotaur and was captured by Heracles.

clue.text: Increased beauty

definitions.meaning: went up, past tense of the verb to go up
a flower prized for its loveliness, or a lovely person

explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, meaning increased, and a rose is a classic emblem of beauty.

clue.text: A number of birds hide round back of house

indicators.note: round means the word for hide goes around the letter

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of house

explanation.surface: Some birds conceal themselves around the rear of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives E; 'round' puts SKIN around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a flock of wild geese or ducks in flight, a collective noun.

clue.text: Where large vehicles kept swerving initially into Cornish town pool

indicators.note: into means the first letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of swerving is used

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money staked, a kitty

explanation.surface: Lorries veer at first into a swimming pool in a Cornish resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDE is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England; 'initially' gives S and 'into' puts it inside BUDE. 'pool' is the kitty, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus depot is a garage where a fleet of buses is parked and serviced.

clue.text: Swim in sauce

definitions.meaning: a thick savoury mixture for scooping with crisps

explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a quick swim and also a thick sauce for dunking food into.

clue.text: Caught with pain, ultimately was sick

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of pain is taken

parts.note: ailed means was unwell

explanation.surface: Someone caught a bug, was in pain and finally fell ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives N from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed is slang for caught or arrested, as a culprit is pinned down.

clue.text: Exuberant mole grabbing forty winks

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for mole holds the nap inside it

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation
kip is British slang for a nap or short sleep

explanation.surface: A lively burrowing animal snatches a quick nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the burrowing animal; it is the planted secret agent. 'forty winks' is a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Skippy means bouncing and full of energy, like someone skipping along.

clue.text: Horse, a grey perhaps, holding nothing back

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters keep the reversed word inside
perhaps means the letters of a grey could be ordered otherwise
back means the word for nothing is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A horse, possibly a grey, holding nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grey perhaps' looks like a definition by example of the horse; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal on A GREY, giving YEARG, and 'back' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old.
